interpretations: Overall average modulation index is computed across all signals that successfully join to a telescope and observatory (inner join). Groups are (telescope, weather profile). Keep groups whose average modulation index is strictly above that overall average. Then, per weather profile, report the average of the kept groups' average modulation index, the average of their average phase shift, and the average of (group average modulation index − overall average). Averages are taken over groups (an average of group averages).

Same as 1, but the per-weather-profile figures are computed over the underlying signals of the kept groups (signal-weighted averages) rather than averaging the group averages. The "how far above" value is the average modulation index minus the overall average.
Same as 1, but the overall average modulation index is the average of the group-level averages (each telescope/weather group counted once), not the average across all joined signals.
Same as 1, but the overall average modulation index is taken over all signals in the signals table, including those that don't match a telescope or observatory.
Same as 1, but "above" means greater than or equal to the overall average.

Same as 1, but the overall average modulation index is computed per weather profile (the average across joined signals within that weather profile), and groups are compared with their own weather profile's average. The "how far above" value is measured against that per-weather-profile average.

Same as 1, but the "how far above the overall average on average" is the difference between the weather profile's average modulation index (of kept groups) and the overall average, which is the same as the average of the group differences. It is one value per weather profile.
Same as 1, but the "how far above" is a percentage or ratio above the overall average (relative difference) instead of an absolute difference.
Same as 1, but groups with NULL modulation index or NULL phase shift are handled differently. Either NULLs are ignored in each average separately, or only signals with both values non-null are used.
Same as 1, but the result also includes the telescope in the output (one row per kept telescope/weather group) instead of one row per weather profile.

Same as 1, but the join to observatories goes through the telescope's observatory station (signals → telescopes → observatories), with signals that have no telescope or no observatory dropped. Signals with a NULL weather profile are either excluded or shown as their own group.

Same as 1, but the "how far above" value is the average, over the kept groups, of the group's modulation index minus the overall average, computed as an average of signal-level differences (each signal's modulation index minus the overall average) rather than group-level differences.
Same as 1, but the final per-weather-profile output also includes the number of kept groups, or the telescope list, alongside the averages.
Same as 1, but the comparison "above the overall average" uses the overall average of the groups' phase shift, or applies to both modulation index and phase shift, instead of modulation index only.

Same as 1, but the overall average modulation index is computed across all joined signals that have a non-null weather profile only, so the baseline excludes signals whose observatory has no weather profile.
queries:
WITH base AS (
  SELECT t.telescregistry AS tele, o.weathprofile AS wp, s.modindex AS modindex, s.phaseshiftdeg AS phaseshift
  FROM signals s
  JOIN telescopes t ON s.telescref = t.telescregistry
  JOIN observatories o ON t.observstation = o.observstation
),
overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(modindex) AS overall_avg FROM base
),
groups AS (
  SELECT tele, wp, AVG(modindex) AS avg_mod, AVG(phaseshift) AS avg_phase
  FROM base
  GROUP BY tele, wp
)
SELECT g.wp AS weathprofile,
       AVG(g.avg_mod) AS avg_modindex,
       AVG(g.avg_phase) AS avg_phaseshift,
       AVG(g.avg_mod - ov.overall_avg) AS avg_diff
FROM groups g
CROSS JOIN overall ov
WHERE g.avg_mod > ov.overall_avg
GROUP BY g.wp;
WITH base AS (
  SELECT o.weathprofile, s.modindex
  FROM signals s
  JOIN telescopes t ON s.telescref = t.telescregistry
  JOIN observatories o ON t.observstation = o.observstation
),
overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(modindex) AS m FROM signals
),
kept AS (
  SELECT weathprofile
  FROM base
  GROUP BY weathprofile
  HAVING AVG(modindex) > (SELECT m FROM overall)
)
SELECT b.weathprofile,
       AVG(b.modindex) AS avg_modindex,
       AVG(b.modindex) - (SELECT m FROM overall) AS above_overall
FROM base b
WHERE b.weathprofile IN (SELECT weathprofile FROM kept)
GROUP BY b.weathprofile;
WITH g AS (
  SELECT s.telescref AS telescref, o.weathprofile AS weathprofile, AVG(s.modindex) AS avg_modindex
  FROM signals s
  JOIN telescopes t ON s.telescref = t.telescregistry
  JOIN observatories o ON t.observstation = o.observstation
  GROUP BY s.telescref, o.weathprofile
)
SELECT telescref, weathprofile, avg_modindex, (SELECT AVG(avg_modindex) FROM g) AS overall_avg_modindex
FROM g;
SELECT o.observstation
FROM observatories o
JOIN telescopes t ON t.observstation = o.observstation
JOIN signals s ON s.telescref = t.telescregistry
GROUP BY o.observstation
HAVING AVG(s.modindex) > (SELECT AVG(modindex) FROM signals);
WITH joined AS (
  SELECT o.observstation, o.weathprofile, s.modindex
  FROM signals s
  JOIN telescopes t ON s.telescref = t.telescregistry
  JOIN observatories o ON t.observstation = o.observstation
),
wp_avg AS (
  SELECT weathprofile, AVG(modindex) AS overall_avg
  FROM joined
  GROUP BY weathprofile
),
grp AS (
  SELECT observstation, weathprofile, AVG(modindex) AS group_avg
  FROM joined
  GROUP BY observstation, weathprofile
)
SELECT g.observstation, g.weathprofile, g.group_avg, w.overall_avg, g.group_avg - w.overall_avg AS above_avg
FROM grp g
JOIN wp_avg w ON g.weathprofile = w.weathprofile
WHERE g.group_avg > w.overall_avg;
